mainTopic: The exemption of בעליו עמו: whether it covers a שומר חנם, the refutation of רב המנונא's strict conditions, and how אביי derives from the פסוקים that the time of borrowing is what counts.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a rejected proof. Our משנה lists only the שואל, whose exemption when the owner is with him is written openly in the Torah, so its silence about a שומר חנם proves nothing. A ברייתא about borrowing or renting an animal together with its owner is then tried as a proof. It is pushed away, because it could follow רבי מאיר, or a reversed version of the opinions, where a שוכר counts as a שומר חנם. Next, רב המנונא rules that the borrower is exempt only if the owner does the same work as his animal, the whole time from the borrowing until the mishap. רבא challenges him from the same ברייתא, and its wording shows the owner can be doing different work. Two more ברייתות show that being with the borrower at the time of borrowing, or even for one moment after the handover, is enough. So רב המנונא is refuted. Finally, the גמרא begins explaining how the פסוקים teach this: אביי reads them like רבי יאשיה, and the time of borrowing turns out to be what counts.

steps.title: The משנה only lists what the Torah writes openly
steps.stepSummary: An earlier proof from the משנה is rejected. The משנה only teaches cases written openly in the Torah, not cases learned through a דרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is written openly, the משנה teaches; what comes from a דרשה, it does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes pushing away an earlier proof. The משנה does not mention a שומר חנם simply because it only lists cases the Torah writes openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof argued that the משנה's silence about a שומר חנם shows the exemption does not cover negligence. The answer is that the exemption for a שואל is written openly in the פסוק. Any other שומר would only come from a דרשה, which this משנה does not bother to list. So the silence proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, clearly (written in the פסוק itself)
From a דרשה, an interpretation of the פסוק
The owner is with it (working for the borrower), which brings an exemption

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an argument that started before this section. It is not a new rule about the Torah; it only explains why the משנה chose to list some cases and not others.

phrases.english: What is written explicitly – he teaches,
phrases.notes: He means the שואל, whose exemption when the owner is with him is written right in the פסוק (שמות 22:14).

phrases.english: what comes from interpretation – he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיבָא בְּהֶדְיָא – קָתָנֵי, דְּאָתְיָא מִדְּרָשָׁא – לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a proof attempt from the משנה that began before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה's silence about a שומר חנם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה lists every case where the exemption applies. In fact it lists only cases written openly in the Torah.

steps.title: A ברייתא with four combinations of borrowing and renting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: whether the animal and its owner were borrowed or rented, in any combination, the person is exempt if the animal dies, even when the owner worked somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he borrowed the animal and borrowed its owner with it, or rented it and hired its owner, or borrowed it and hired its owner, or rented it and borrowed its owner, he is exempt if it dies. This is true even if the owner was doing the work in a different place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, to try to answer the question again. This step only quotes the source; the argument from it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes beyond the משנה. It also includes someone who RENTED the animal (a שוכר), not just a borrower. Whether a שוכר counts as a paid or unpaid שומר will decide what this ברייתא proves.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁאָלָהּ וְשָׁאַל בְּעָלֶיהָ עִמָּהּ,
phrases.english: Come and hear: If he borrowed it and borrowed its owner with it,
phrases.notes: "It" is an animal, like the cow talked about in this פרק.

phrases.english: rented it and hired its owner with it,
borrowed it and hired its owner with it,
rented it and borrowed its owner with it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.english: even though the owner was doing work in another place,
and it died – he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה fails, the גמרא turns to a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the exemption of בעליו עמו covers a שומר חנם, which would mean it covers negligence.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing four combinations of borrowing and renting the animal and its owner.

steps.title: Read as רבי יהודה, the ברייתא seems to leave out the שומר חנם
steps.stepSummary: The scholars assumed the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who treats a שוכר like a שומר שכר. Then this תנא does list a derived case, the שומר שכר, yet still leaves out the שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed: whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה, who says a renter is like a paid שומר. So this תנא does teach a case learned from a דרשה, and still he does not teach the שומר חנם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds the proof from the ברייתא. If a שוכר is a שומר שכר, the ברייתא is willing to list derived cases, so leaving out the שומר חנם must mean something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1's defense was that a תנא only lists cases written openly. This ברייתא, read according to רבי יהודה, lists a שומר שכר, which only comes from a דרשה. Since it is willing to list derived cases but skips the שומר חנם, it seems the exemption does not apply to him. That would mean it does not cover negligence.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid guardian (liable for theft and loss)
An unpaid guardian (liable only for negligence)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a dispute about the status of a שוכר can decide what a ברייתא proves about a completely different question.

phrases.aramaic: סַבְרוּהָ הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: They assumed: whose is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: a renter is like a paid guardian!
And look, this תנא teaches
a matter that comes from interpretation,
phrases.notes: That is the שומר שכר; the Torah only writes the exemption openly for a borrower.

phrases.english: whereas an unpaid guardian he does not teach!

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְרוּהָ הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 2, and gets around the defense given in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the exemption of בעליו עמו does not apply to a שומר חנם, and so does not cover negligence.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא read according to רבי יהודה, where it lists a derived case (the שומר שכר) but leaves out the שומר חנם.

steps.title: Read as רבי מאיר, the ברייתא is about a שומר חנם
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא may follow רבי מאיר, who treats a שוכר like a שומר חנם. Then it does teach the שומר חנם, and the same law would apply to a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי מאיר, who says a renter is like an unpaid שומר. So the תנא taught the שומר חנם, and the same is true of a paid שומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by reading the ברייתא according to a different תנא. Then the ברייתא is not silent about the שומר חנם at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, the renter in the ברייתא IS a שומר חנם, so the ברייתא teaches that he is exempt. That would actually mean the exemption covers negligence. Since we do not know whether the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה or רבי מאיר, no proof can be drawn either way.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves nothing. Under רבי יהודה (renter = paid שומר) it seems to leave out the שומר חנם. Under רבי מאיר (renter = unpaid שומר) it includes him. The question of negligence stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. רבי יהודה says a renter is like a PAID שומר. רבי מאיר says a renter is like an UNPAID שומר.

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: a renter is like an unpaid guardian,
and the תנא taught the unpaid guardian,
and the same is true for a paid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 3 by giving another possible author for the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא in step 3.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. It could follow רבי מאיר, and then it explicitly includes the שומר חנם.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the author of the ברייתא is unclear, it cannot settle whether בעליו עמו exempts negligence.

steps.title: A second rejection: the opinions are reversed
steps.stepSummary: Another way to reject the proof: רבה בר אבוה reverses the opinions, so רבי יהודה holds that a שוכר is like a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say it as רבה בר אבוה taught it with the opinions switched: How does a renter pay? רבי מאיר says: like a paid guard. רבי יהודה says: like an unpaid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to knock down the proof from Step 3. Even if the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, he may hold that a שוכר is like a שומר חנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3's proof needed רבי יהודה to treat a שוכר like a שומר שכר. רבה בר אבוה's version switches the two opinions, so רבי יהודה treats a שוכר like a שומר חנם. Then the ברייתא really does teach the שומר חנם, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
A renter, someone who pays to use an item
An unpaid guard, who is responsible only for carelessness

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In Step 4 the usual version was used, where רבי מאיר says a שוכר is like a שומר חנם. Here רבה בר אבוה's version gives that view to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: If you wish, say
as Rabba bar Avuh reversed it and taught:
phrases.notes: He switches which opinion belongs to רבי מאיר and which belongs to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: How does a renter pay?
Rabbi Meir says: like a paid guard;
Rabbi Yehuda says: like an unpaid guard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כִּדְמַחְלֵיף רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ וְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent rejection of the proof in Step 3, alongside Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof even if the ברייתא is assumed to follow רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי יהודה treats a שוכר like a שומר שכר. In רבה בר אבוה's version he treats a שוכר like a שומר חנם.

steps.title: רב המנונא: the exemption applies only with the same work for the whole time
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא limits the exemption of בעליו עמו. The owner must work with his own animal in the same job, from the moment of borrowing until it breaks or dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: A borrower is always liable, unless it is a cow and the owner plows with it, or a donkey and the owner drives it from behind. And the owner must be working from the time of borrowing until the time it broke or died. So he holds that 'its owner is with him' means for the whole matter.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב המנונא sets strict conditions for when a borrower is exempt because the owner is working with him. The גמרא then explains the reasoning behind his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two conditions. First, the owner must be doing the same work as his animal, like plowing with the cow. Second, he must be working the whole time, from the borrowing until the damage. The גמרא infers that he reads the words בעליו עמו as covering the entire matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Drives a donkey by walking behind it
Its owner is with him: the Torah's source for the exemption

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the strict standard for the exemption of בעליו עמו, and the rest of the סוגיא tests it.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
He is always liable
unless it is a cow and he plows with it,
or a donkey and he drives it from behind,
and unless the owner is working
from the time of borrowing
until the time it breaks a limb or dies.
Evidently he holds that 'its owner is with him'
means for the whole matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: לְעוֹלָם הוּא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the limits of the exemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The borrower is exempt only if the owner does the same work as his animal for the entire period, from the borrowing until it breaks or dies.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the ברייתא: the owner worked elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the ברייתא, which exempts the borrower even when the owner worked 'in another place,' and suggests this means different work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: If he borrowed it and borrowed its owner, rented it and hired its owner, rented it and borrowed its owner, or borrowed it and hired its owner, then even though the owner was working in another place and it died, he is exempt. Isn't that talking about different work?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא uses the same ברייתא from Step 2 to attack רב המנונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא exempts the borrower even when the owner worked 'in another place.' רבא reads this as the owner doing a different job from his animal. That would contradict רב המנונא's first condition, that the owner must do the same work.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (pushes for a reading)

phrases.english: Rava objected:
If he borrowed it and borrowed its owner with it,
rented it and hired its owner with it,
rented it and borrowed its owner with it,
borrowed it and hired its owner with it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה
phrases.english: even though the owner was doing work
in another place, and it died, he is exempt.
Isn't it talking about 'different work'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב המנונא's ruling from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's requirement that the owner do the same work as the animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא exempts the borrower when the owner works 'in another place,' which seems to mean different work.

steps.title: No, it is the same work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about the owner doing the same work as the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the same work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב המנונא by reading the ברייתא as the owner doing the same job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא means the same work, it does not contradict רב המנונא at all. This answer still has to explain the words 'another place,' and the next step asks about that.

phrases.english: No, it is about the same work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the source
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner is doing the same job as his animal.

steps.title: Then what does 'another place' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if it is the same work, why does the ברייתא say 'another place'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what does 'another place' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer and sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing the same job sounds like working right next to the animal. So the words 'another place' need explaining.

phrases.english: But then, what is 'another place'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא means the same work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Same work seems to mean the same place, so why does the ברייתא say 'another place'?

steps.title: The owner breaks up the soil ahead of the animal
steps.stepSummary: The owner loosens the soil while walking in front of the animal. It is the same job, done in a different spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he loosens the soil and walks ahead of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains 'another place': the owner works on the same plowing job, but ahead of the animal instead of right beside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking up the hard soil in front of the animal is part of the same plowing work. So the ברייתא fits רב המנונא, and רבא's challenge is answered.
steps.whatToRemember: For now, רב המנונא is defended: 'another place' can mean the same job, done a little ahead of the animal. Step 11 challenges this answer, and step 13 knocks it down.

phrases.english: Where he loosens the soil and walks ahead of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 9 and finishes the defense of רב המנונא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Another place' means a different job, away from the animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the same job, done just ahead of the animal.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא shows the first half means different work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the סיפא of the ברייתא says the owner worked 'alongside' the animal. That suggests the רישא, which says 'in another place,' is about different work. This goes against רב המנונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the second half of the ברייתא talks about the owner working right alongside the animal. That shows the first half is about different work. The second half says: if he borrowed the animal and only afterward borrowed the owner, or rented the animal and only afterward hired the owner with it, then even though the owner was plowing right alongside it, if it died the borrower is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 10. It uses the wording of the second half of the same ברייתא as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the גמרא said 'another place' still means the same job, like loosening the soil in front of the animal. But the סיפא uses a different phrase, 'alongside it,' for the same job. If 'alongside it' means the same work, then the different phrase in the רישא, 'another place,' should mean different work. If so, the borrower is exempt even when the owner does different work, which goes against רב המנונא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first half of a משנה or ברייתא
The second half of a משנה or ברייתא
Literally 'on its back'; working right alongside the animal

phrases.english: But since the latter clause is about 'alongside it'
the first clause must be about different work
as the latter clause teaches:
if he borrowed it and afterward borrowed its owner

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכָרָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׂכַר בְּעָלֶיהָ עִמָּהּ
phrases.english: or rented it and afterward hired its owner with it

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים חוֹרְשִׁין עַל גַּבָּהּ
phrases.english: even though the owner was plowing alongside it
and it died, he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 10 by comparing it with the wording of the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 10 that 'another place' in the רישא still means the same work, and with it רב המנונא's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא uses 'alongside it' for the same work. So the different wording in the רישא, 'another place,' points to different work.

steps.title: Both halves are about the same work, and each teaches its own new point
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that both halves of the ברייתא are about the same work. The רישא teaches that the borrower is exempt even when the owner was not right alongside the animal, because the owner was working for him at the time of borrowing. The סיפא teaches that the borrower is liable even when the owner was right alongside, because the owner was not working for him at the time of borrowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: both halves are about the same work, and each half teaches a new point. The first half teaches that even though the owner was not right alongside the animal, only doing the same job, he is exempt, because the owner was working for him at the time of borrowing. The second half teaches that even though the owner was right alongside it, he is liable, because the owner was not working for him at the time of borrowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains that the two halves use different wording to make the strongest point possible in each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer says the wording is not about different work versus same work. The רישא picks the weaker case, the owner not right alongside, to show the borrower is still exempt. The סיפא picks the stronger case, the owner right alongside, to show the borrower is still liable. The deciding factor in both is whether the owner was working for the borrower at the moment of borrowing.

keyTerms.meaning: In the same work as the animal
A new point; something we would not have known on our own
At the time of the borrowing
Exempt; he does not have to pay

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the key moment for בעליו עמו is the time of borrowing. Where exactly the owner was working matters less.

phrases.english: They say: the first clause and the latter clause are both about the same work
and the first clause teaches us a new point
and the latter clause teaches us a new point.
The first clause teaches us a new point

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו עַל גַּבָּהּ
phrases.english: that even though he was not alongside it
but only in the same work

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּהֲווֹ בְּעָלִים בִּשְׁעַת שְׁאֵילָה – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: since the owner was with him at the time of borrowing, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: 'Was with him' means the owner was already working for the borrower when the animal was borrowed.

phrases.english: And the latter clause teaches us a new point
that even though he was alongside it

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הֲווֹ בְּעָלִים בִּשְׁעַת שְׁאֵילָה – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: since the owner was not with him at the time of borrowing, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by explaining the different wording in each half.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each half picks the strongest example to make its own new point (רבותא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The different wording in the two halves means the רישא is about different work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both halves are about the same work. The wording only shows how far each rule goes: exempt even when not right alongside, liable even when right alongside.

steps.title: The answer fails: if both halves are the same work, there is no new point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer of step 12. A new point makes sense only if the רישא is about different work and the סיפא about the same work. If both are about the same work, the change in wording teaches nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this?! It works fine if you say the first half is about different work and the second half is about the same work, because that is a real new point. But if you say both halves are about the same work, what is the new point? Both cases are the same work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the answer it just gave. It says the 'new point' idea only works if the two halves are about different kinds of work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real new point needs a real difference between the cases. If the רישא is different work and the סיפא is same work, the ברייתא teaches that the type of work does not matter, only the time of borrowing. If both are the same work, the wording difference adds nothing. So the ברייתא seems to say the borrower is exempt even with different work, which goes against רב המנונא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this?! A strong rejection of what was just said
It works fine if you say
This one and that one; both cases

steps.whatToRemember: The רישא of the ברייתא must be about different work, so the borrower is exempt even when the owner does a different job, as long as the owner was working for him at the time of borrowing. This knocks down the first part of רב המנונא's rule, the same-work condition.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 13 does not attack the ברייתא. It attacks the answer from step 12, which tried to read both halves as the same work.

phrases.english: What is this?!

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רֵישָׁא בִּמְלָאכָה אַחֶרֶת
phrases.english: It works fine if you say the first clause is about different work
and the latter clause is about the same work, because that is the new point.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא בְּאוֹתָהּ מְלָאכָה
phrases.english: But if you say the first clause and the latter clause are both about the same work
what is the new point?
This one and that one are both about the same work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 12 and brings back the challenge of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The answer that both halves of the ברייתא are about the same work.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If both halves are the same work, the change in wording teaches nothing new. A real new point needs the רישא to be about different work.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that being there at the time of borrowing is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that if the owner was with the borrower at the time of borrowing, the borrower is exempt even if the owner was not there when the animal was injured or died. This goes against רב המנונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, a ברייתא teaches: The Torah says 'If its owner is with him, he shall not pay.' From that, don't I already know that if the owner is not with him, he must pay? So why does the Torah bother to write 'its owner is not with him'? To teach you this: if the owner was with him when the animal was borrowed, he does not need to be with him when it was injured or died. But if he was with him when it was injured or died, he must also have been with him when it was borrowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב המנונא. This time it attacks his rule that the owner must be working for the borrower the whole time, from borrowing until the mishap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sees an extra פסוק and learns a rule from it. What counts is the time of borrowing. If the owner was there at the borrowing, that alone exempts the borrower. רב המנונא said the owner had to be there from borrowing all the way to the mishap, so this ברייתא contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. It introduces another challenge.
Why does the פסוק need to say this? It is asking about extra wording.
Injured or died. These are the mishaps a borrower normally pays for.

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves are not equal. Being there at the borrowing is enough by itself. Being there at the mishap is enough only if the owner was also there at the borrowing.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught in a ברייתא:
From the implication of what is stated:
"If its owner is with him, he shall not pay"

phrases.aramaic: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאִם בְּעָלָיו אֵין עִמּוֹ
phrases.english: do I not know that if its owner is not with him
he must surely pay?
Rather, why does the פסוק say
"its owner is not with him"? To tell you:
If he was with him at the time of borrowing,
he does not need to be with him
at the time it was injured or died.
If he was with him at the time it was injured or died,
he needs to have been with him at the time of borrowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to רב המנונא, aimed at a different part of his rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's rule that the owner must work for the borrower from the time of borrowing until the mishap.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says presence at the time of borrowing alone is enough to exempt, so there is no need for the owner to be there the whole time.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says even one moment with the owner exempts
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא learns from the other extra פסוק that once the animal leaves the lender's hands with the owner working for the borrower even for one moment, the borrower is exempt if it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: The Torah says 'If its owner is not with him, he must surely pay.' From that, don't I already know that if the owner is with him, he does not pay? So why does the Torah write 'If its owner is with him'? To tell you: once the animal left the lender's domain with its owner working for the borrower even for one moment, and then it died, the borrower is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that pushes the same idea even further against רב המנונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא also learns from a פסוק that seems extra. Even one moment of the owner working for the borrower after the animal was handed over is enough to exempt. That clearly goes against רב המנונא's demand that the owner be there for the whole time.

keyTerms.meaning: The domain of the lender, meaning the owner
One moment, even a short time
Exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches:
From the implication of what is stated:
"Its owner is not with him, he must surely pay"

phrases.aramaic: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאִם בְּעָלָיו עִמּוֹ לֹא יְשַׁלֵּם?
phrases.english: do I not know that if its owner is with him, he does not pay?
Rather, why does the פסוק say
"If its owner is with him"? To tell you:
once it left the domain of the lender
with the owner, even for one moment,
phrases.notes: "With the owner" means the owner was working for the borrower during that moment.

phrases.english: and then it died, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא that strengthens the challenge of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's requirement that the owner be there from borrowing until the mishap.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even one moment of the owner working with the borrower is enough to exempt, so the whole span cannot be required.

steps.title: רב המנונא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that these ברייתות are a real refutation of רב המנונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב המנונא. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that רב המנונא's view has been disproven by the ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיובתא is the strongest form of rejection. It means the opinion cannot stand against an earlier source. Saying it twice confirms there is no answer left.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation from an earlier source

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה does not follow רב המנונא, and both of his conditions fall. The owner does not need to do the same work as his animal (steps 11-13). He also does not need to be working for the borrower the whole time: being there at the borrowing, or even for one moment after the handover, can be enough to exempt the borrower (steps 14-15).

phrases.english: This is a refutation of רב המנונא.
It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from the two ברייתות.

steps.title: אביי follows רבי יאשיה and רבא follows רבי יונתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces two ways to read the פסוקים: אביי reads them like רבי יאשיה, and רבא reads them like רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי holds like רבי יאשיה and explains the פסוקים like רבי יאשיה. רבא holds like רבי יונתן and explains the פסוקים like רבי יונתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It names two אמוראים who will each explain how the ברייתא learns its rule from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן argue about how to read a law in the Torah that mentions two details together. רבי יאשיה says both details must be present. רבי יונתן says one is enough. Here the two details are being with the borrower at the time of borrowing and at the time of the mishap.

phrases.english: אביי holds like רבי יאשיה,
phrases.notes: רבי יאשיה reads two details listed together as meaning both are needed (94b). Here they are borrowing time and mishap time.

phrases.english: and explains the פסוקים like רבי יאשיה.
רבא holds like רבי יונתן,
and explains the פסוקים like רבי יונתן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the refutation to explaining how the ברייתא gets its rule from the פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי reads the פסוקים like רבי יאשיה, and רבא reads them like רבי יונתן.

steps.title: אביי's reading: liable only when the owner was absent at both times
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads 'its owner is not with him, he must pay' like רבי יאשיה. The borrower pays only if the owner was absent at both times. If the owner was there at one of the times, the borrower is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי holds like רבי יאשיה and explains the פסוקים like רבי יאשיה: 'Its owner is not with him, he must surely pay.' The reason he pays is that the owner was not there at both times. So if the owner was there at one time and not the other, the borrower is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out אביי's reading of the פסוק about paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי יאשיה, 'not with him' means not there at borrowing and not there at the mishap. Only then must the borrower pay. If the owner was there at either one of those times, the borrower does not pay.

keyTerms.meaning: At both of them, meaning both times

phrases.english: אביי holds like רבי יאשיה
and explains the פסוקים like רבי יאשיה:
"Its owner is not with him, he must surely pay".
The reason is that he was not there at both,
phrases.notes: "Both" means the time of borrowing and the time of the mishap.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אִיתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא וְלֵיתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: but if he was there at one and not at the other, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins carrying out the plan of step 17 with אביי's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, the borrower pays only if the owner was absent both at borrowing and at the mishap. If the owner was there at one of these times, the borrower is exempt.

steps.title: The second verse seems to require the owner at both times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's reading. The פסוק 'if its owner is with him, he does not pay' suggests the borrower is exempt only when the owner was there at both times, so being there at just one time should make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written, 'If its owner is with him, he does not pay'? That suggests the reason he is exempt is that the owner was there at both times. So if the owner was there at one time and not the other, the borrower should be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with what אביי just said. A different פסוק seems to teach the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, the first פסוק was read to mean the borrower pays only if the owner was missing at both times, so one time is enough to exempt. The second פסוק, read the same way, means he is exempt only if the owner was present at both times, so one time is not enough. The two פסוקים now seem to clash about the case where the owner was there at only one time.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason. The גמרא uses it to draw an inference from the wording.
He was there at both times.
At one time but not at the other.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"If its owner is with him, he does not pay"?
The reason he is exempt is that the owner was there at both times.
phrases.notes: "Both" means both the time of borrowing and the time the animal was injured or died.

phrases.english: This implies that if he was there at one time
and not at the other, the borrower is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reading from step 18 by using the other פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading, following רבי יאשיה, that the owner's presence at one time is enough to exempt the borrower.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the inference from 'not with him' is read as 'both times absent', then the inference from 'with him' must be read as 'both times present'. The two inferences contradict each other when the owner was there at only one time.

steps.title: The time of borrowing is what counts
steps.stepSummary: The two times are not equal. If the owner was with the borrower at the time of borrowing, the borrower is exempt even if the owner was not there at the injury or death. If the owner was there only at the injury or death, he also had to be there at the borrowing for the exemption to apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse comes to tell you this. If the owner was with him at the time of borrowing, he does not need to be with him at the time of injury or death. If he was with him at the time of injury or death, he still needs to have been with him at the time of borrowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining which 'one time' each פסוק is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק describes a different 'one time' case. Presence at the borrowing alone exempts the borrower, which fits the first פסוק. Presence at the injury or death alone does not exempt him, which fits the second פסוק. So the clash disappears, because the time of borrowing is the deciding factor.

keyTerms.meaning: To tell you. This introduces what the פסוק comes to teach.
The time the animal was injured or died.
He must be with him, meaning the owner must be working for the borrower.

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, reading like רבי יאשיה: if the owner was there at the borrowing, the borrower is exempt. If the owner was there only at the injury or death, the borrower is liable.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 18 said 'there at one of the times exempts.' That is now narrowed down: only the time of borrowing works alone. Being there only at the injury or death does not exempt the borrower.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the comparison with רבא's reading like רבי יונתן. The two readings differ on how much weight each time carries.

phrases.english: The verse comes to tell you:
If he was with him at the time of borrowing,
phrases.notes: "With him" means the owner was working for the borrower.

phrases.english: he does not need to be with him
at the time the animal is injured or dies.
But if he was with him at the time it was injured or died,
he needs to have been with him at the time of borrowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases. The two 'one time' cases are not the same: presence at the borrowing differs from presence at the injury or death.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Presence at any one of the two times would have the same effect, so the two פסוקים contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Presence at the time of borrowing alone exempts the borrower. Presence only at the time of injury or death does not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In אביי's reading, the time of borrowing decides whether the borrower is exempt.
